scope: QA only; four user supplied reference decks; extend existing native engine

acceptance.criterion: Source-pinned executable effects, explicit prerequisites and partial support; promotion requires independent positive/negative test evidence
Real fixture mechanics execute with colored resource conservation, conditional trigger gates and exact costs; source counts do not substitute for behavior
Bounded action traces with starting state, prerequisite rejection, no victory from assembly; integrated assistant tool
Measured native/reference scenarios and honest unavailable external engines; no synthetic engine timings
Visible-hand-only decisions, strategy-aware sequencing and adversarial cases; no hidden-information leakage
Metric-specific dependency evidence when justified, legacy failclosed fallback and no unknown metrics presented as improvement
Targeted regression suites, independent review and actual fixture/browser checks; source deck unchanged and max3 swaps in 3 copies

gates: Never infer rules correctness from model confidence
Never mark a whole card supported because one effect executes
Never infer win rate or deck superiority from engine-event proxies
Compare matching engine/settings versions; rerun baselines after mechanics changes
remaining_gaps: Full MTG coverage is not achieved. General combat, stack responses, replacement effects, trigger multipliers and many card abilities remain unmodeled.
Source-known combo claims and bounded hypothetical models do not prove whole-deck consistency or wins.
Opening comparability remains conservative for unknown card swaps; unsupported dependency claims never authorize score comparisons.
Native arbitrary-state differential replay remains a follow-up; Forge currently validates separately against the shared fixture expectations.
Starter source corpus is bounded to 183 variants, not the entire Commander Spellbook catalog.
